chunks: Uthman ibn Isa from Umayr ibn Adhinah from Sulayman ibn Qays said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Verily Allah has forbidden Paradise to every foul-mouthed, shameless person who does not care about what he utters and what is said to him. For if you investigate him, you will not find him except as a babler or a partner of Satan.
A man asked: O Messenger of Allah, are there really people who are partners of Satan?
He replied: Do you not read the statement of Allah: 'And partner with them in their wealth and children'?
Then it was asked: And are there [really] some people who do not care about what they utter or what is said to them?

He said: Yes. He who exposes himself to the people and speaks [negatively] about them while he knows that they will not leave him [and will react against what he has said]; such a person does not care about what he utters and what is said to utters and what is said to him.

key_terms.تَعَرَّضَ لِلنَّاسِ: Exposed himself to the people (for criticism)

ai.seo_question: Who are considered 'partners of Satan' in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* emphasizes that Paradise is forbidden to the foul-mouthed and shameless, defining 'Satan's partner' not merely as idolaters but as those who engage in reciprocal slander, knowing their words will rebound upon them. The Imam clarifies this by linking the trait of indifference to speech with the Quranic concept of sharing in wealth and offspring, suggesting that verbal abuse creates a spiritual partnership with Satan through the erosion of social bonds. This interpretation highlights the Shia emphasis on *adab al-kalam* (etiquette of speech) as a key determinant of spiritual status.
